sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Western blot with anti-Flag antibody confirmed expression of the tagged full-length protein in stable cell clones (L2). No surface trafficking assay or enzymatic activity assay reported for the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: ECE-1 is a type II transmembrane metalloprotease with a large extracellular ectodomain (residues 90–770); the C-terminus at W770 is extracellular and is the only extracellular terminus. Python verification confirms seq[769]='W' and len=770. The paper explicitly states the tag is on the 'C-terminal end' of the full-length membrane-anchored protein, leaving no ambiguity about which terminus carries the tag. Validation is limited to Western blot detection; no surface or functional assay was reported for the tagged construct. Full-length ECE-1c with a C-terminal Myc/Flag tag expressed via a pLVX-IRES-mCherry bicistronic lentiviral vector in stable mammalian cell clones (PMC11515556). ECE1 is a type II single-pass TM protein; the C-terminus (residue 770, W) lies entirely within the extracellular ectodomain (residues 90–770), 681 residues from the TM boundary. The paper names 'C-terminal end' of the full-length protein with no specific residue number; topology gives exactly one extracellular C-terminal junction.

sources.claim: For obtention of stable cell clones overexpressing Myc/Flag-tagged (C-terminal end) ECE-1c forms, a pLVX-IRES-mCherry bicistronic lentiviral vector (Takara Bio, CA, USA) was used.

literature_notes: The ledger contains two clips (L1, L2) both from PMC11515556, both describing the same C-terminal Myc/Flag-tagged ECE-1c construct. L1 describes the construct design; L2 describes Western blot confirmation of expression. Both ground the same single site. No internal loop insertions, N-terminal tags, or other isoform-specific sites are reported in the ledger. Confidence is medium rather than high because (1) no specific residue number is cited (position is topology-derived), (2) only Western blot detection was reported — no surface trafficking (flow cytometry, immunofluorescence) or enzymatic activity assay was performed on the tagged construct, and (3) the isoform is ECE-1c, which differs from the canonical isoform a in its N-terminal cytoplasmic tail, but shares the same C-terminus (W770 in canonical numbering).
